title: 1992 AHSME Problem 14
statement: Which of the following equations have the same graph? \[ \begin{aligned} &\text{I. }y=x-2\\ &\text{II. }y=\dfrac{x^2-4}{x+2}\\ &\text{III. }(x+2)y=x^2-4 \end{aligned} \]

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
None. All the equations have different
graphs

solutions.text:
Equation I is the whole line \(y=x-2.\) Equation II simplifies to that line only when \(x\ne-2,\) so it omits \((-2,-4).\) In equation III, every point with \(x=-2\) satisfies \(0=0;\) for other \(x\) it gives \(y=x-2.\) Thus III is the line together with the entire vertical line \(x=-2.\) The three graphs are different.

Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: Pay special attention to what happens when \(x=-2\)
Equation II omits one point, while equation III includes an entire extra vertical line
